title: QuickBridge SDK primer for non-engineers (draft)
content:
Purpose:
This is a working draft of the QuickBridge SDK primer aimed at non-engineer contributors (PMs, designers, solutions consultants) who need to prototype and ship small integrations with Redwood APIs without heavy engineering support. The goal is to shorten discovery -> prototype time from days to hours, reduce handoffs, and collect higher-quality early feedback for eng teams.

Audience:
- Product managers and designers building demos or early integrations.
- Solution engineers who need a predictable quick path to a working demo.
- Internal trial users who want to validate UX patterns without creating infra.

Non-goals:
- Not intended to replace the full SDK docs or deep integration patterns for production.
- Not a secure production deployment guide.

Success metrics (90d):
- 30 internal demos by non-engineers using QuickBridge flows.
- Median time-to-demo <= 3 hours (from readme to working prototype).
- At least 6 usability issues filed in RDW-1423 tag referencing the primer.

What QuickBridge provides (high level):
- Minimal-install SDK wrapper (JS) with opinionated defaults for quick demos: minimal auth, ephemeral keys, pre-configured prompt templates, and a small set of components (chat, summarize, embed-search).
- A small CLI (quickbridge init) that scaffolds a runnable demo and starts a local dev server.
- Example playgrounds (static HTML + tiny JS) that can be shared with stakeholders.

Core flows (user journeys):
1) Demo scaffold (PM/Designer)
   - Install Node or use GitHub Codespaces.
   - Run `npx quickbridge@dev init` and answer 3 prompts (use-case, model profile, demo name).
   - CLI generates /public demo, /src with 2 components: ChatBox and ExamplePromptRunner.
   - `npx quickbridge@dev start` opens a local page with live chat backed by Redwood hosted API (ephemeral key).

2) Interactive prototype (Solutions Engineer)
   - Swap prompt templates in the YAML file, update UI text, test with sample dataset (CSV importer included).
   - Validate latency and token usage from the small telemetry panel.

3) Shareable snapshot (PM)
   - `npx quickbridge snapshot --share` packages the demo and uploads to an internal static host with a short-lived share link.

Minimal security model (for demos):
- Uses ephemeral demo tokens with strict CORS and referrer limits.
- Demo tokens expire in 24 hours and are rate-limited.
- Explicit warning page shown on startup about production readiness.

Quick reference: commands and files
- `npx quickbridge@dev init` -> creates quickbridge.yml, /src/demo.js, /public/index.html
- quickbridge.yml fields: demo_name, model_profile (e.g., redwood-m2-small), template_set, ephemeral_key (auto)
- `npx quickbridge@dev start` -> local dev server at http://localhost:5173
- `npx quickbridge@dev snapshot --share` -> returns share URL

Sample quickbridge.yml (auto-generated snippet):
- demo_name: "jira-summarize-demo"
- model_profile: "redwood-m2-small"
- template_set: "summarize-v1"
- telemetry: true

Example JavaScript usage (conceptual, non-production):
- import QuickBridge from 'quickbridge'
- const qb = new QuickBridge({ephemeralKey: 'auto', profile: 'redwood-m2-small'})
- const summary = await qb.summarizeText(longText)

Telemetry and observability in the primer:
- Light-weight metrics surfaced to the quickbridge console: request latency (p95), tokens per request, error rate.
- Anonymized usage logs (no PII) sent to staging telemetry for prototype-level diagnostics.
- Guidance for escalation: when p95 > 1.5s or token usage is > 3x expectation, open RDW-1423 with reproducible steps.

UX patterns and prompt library (starter set):
- Summarize (long -> bullet list)
- Extract action items (email, owner, due)
- Question-answering over small docset (CSV or short collection)
- Rewriter for tone adjustments

Design checklist for a good demo:
- Single clear call-to-action on first screen
- One primary model-backed interaction (avoid multiplexing features)
- Visible latency indicator and cost hint (approx tokens used)
- Fallback text for rate limits / ephemeral expiry

Rollout plan (3 sprints):
- Sprint 1 (2 weeks): prototype CLI and 3 demo templates; internal dogfood; basic telemetry.
- Sprint 2 (2 weeks): refine onboarding, auth hardening, add CSV importer and snapshot upload.
- Sprint 3 (2 weeks): docs, short training video (5–7m), cross-team demo sessions.

Risks & mitigations:
- Misuse: ephemeral keys limit exposure; include clear guidance that QuickBridge is demo-only.
- Overfitting to hosted API: include a note about differences for Dedicated/Private deployments and how to swap endpoints.
- False assurance of production readiness: add explicit gating checklist and link to full SDK docs.

Open questions (to resolve in RDW-1423):
- What guardrails do we need for sharing snapshot links outside the org?
- Should the CLI create a minimal GitHub repo with CI to allow engineers to pick up demos?
- Which set of model profiles are approved for non-engineer demos?

Next steps (action items):
- [Ava] Build initial npx prototype and push experimental package to npm tag `quickbridge-dev` (ETA: 2024-10-21).
- [Ravi] Draft the 5-minute training video script (ETA: 2024-10-28).
- [Maya] Coordinate two internal pilot sessions with PM/designers (week of 2024-11-04).

Appendix: sample troubleshooting notes (quick):
- 401 ephemeral key errors: run `npx quickbridge auth` or check local firewall blocking outbound connections.
- High token usage: switch template_set to `short-v1` or reduce max_tokens in quickbridge.yml.
- Snapshot upload fails: check internal upload host access and file size (max 10MB).

References and background reading:
- Confluence: QuickBridge-spec-v0.3 (linked above)
- Jira: RDW-1423 (prototype epic)
- GitHub: PR 678 for initial CLI code

Notes to reviewers:
- This is intentionally light on implementation detail; the priority is low-friction adoption for non-engineering stakeholders. Please comment with scenarios we missed (email to #devex or add comments in RDW-1423).
